messages:
Priya: Quick UX thread: compact dashboard rows look noisy when some series use per-row y-axis normalization. Two problems: 1) users expect unit consistency (ms vs %) in the same table, 2) smoothing toggles behave weirdly when normalized. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.example/ux/axis-normalize-issue.png

Noah: Yep. Normalizing helps show trend shape but hides magnitude. For mixed-unit tables we should never normalize by default. Maybe allow "normalize" as an opt-in pill per-column.

Sam (Design): Agree on opt-in. Also propose a small pill next to the column header: "Normalized" (tappable) with a tooltip that says "Compare trend shapes; preserves original units in detail view". For smoothing, toggle should persist per-user preference, not per-row.

Ivy (Eng): Implementation notes: per-column flag is straightforward. We'll render a visual badge and pass a flag to the sparkline renderer. Smoothing persistence can be stored in user prefs. Edge case: when normalized + smoothing both active, we need to clarify in the tooltip how values are computed.

a11y-bot: reminder: ensure the pill has role="switch" and keyboard handlers; tooltip content must be available to screen readers (aria-describedby).

Priya: Copy draft for pill tooltip: "Normalization on: scales each series to [0,1] to compare shapes. Peak magnitude preserved in expanded chart." Any objections to the bracketed [0,1] phrasing?

Noah: Maybe say "scaled to relative range" instead of numeric bracket to avoid implying units. e.g., "scales each series to a relative 000 range to highlight shape; open expanded chart to see absolute values."

Sam (Design): Final decision: opt-in per-column normalize pill with accessible role, smoothing toggle saved in user prefs, tooltip language updated to "scales each series to a relative range to highlight shape; open expanded chart for absolute values." Action items: Sam  update mocks & copy; Ivy  add feature flag and basic impl; Priya  run usability test with 6 users. Target: prototype by next Tuesday.

Priya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
